notes: The same entity as Home Assistant 2026.10.4 sends it with unit_system us_customary: nws.json's values fed to Home Assistant's WeatherEntity as native values in the units its attributes state (°C, hPa, km/h, km, mm), state and forecasts read back through the weather component with hass.config.units set to US_CUSTOMARY_SYSTEM. Temperatures come back as whole °F (ints: outside °C the weather entity rounds to whole degrees), pressure in inHg, wind in mph, visibility in mi and precipitation in in, each to 2 decimals; humidity, bearings, conditions, datetimes and every other field are as in the metric file. The metric file's notes follow; their numbers are metric. State built from the test's DEFAULT_OBSERVATION (tests/components/nws/const.py) run through weather.py in the metric system; the test asserts state 'sunny' and the mock's values, which are changed below. Forecasts are the snapshot's entries, with the numbers changed below. Current conditions never carry dew_point, apparent_temperature, wind_gust_speed, cloud_coverage or uv_index (the code doesn't set them, though the observation has dewpoint, windGust, heatIndex and windChill). Each attribute is present only when the observation has it. No daily forecast: twice_daily (day/night periods, is_daytime) and hourly only. Forecast temperature, dew_point and wind_speed are null when the API omits them; condition is null without an icon; precipitation_probability, humidity and wind_bearing are passed through and can be null. A weather code outside the integration's table passes through as the raw NWS name, so condition can be a non-standard string. Short and detailed text are only in the separate nws.get_forecasts_extra service, not get_forecasts. Changes for realism (test-data artefacts): the mocks fill every reading with 10 in its own unit, so the file had 10 C and 10 % humidity now beside a thunderstorm forecast of 10 F (-12.2 C), dew point 4 F (-15.6 C) and 75 % on an August evening. Humidity 75, 89 %, lightning-rainy and 16.09 km/h from 180 stay in both.
